source: Google's microservices-demo architecture. Every service-to-service call below was also observed in the pre-alert traces of RE2-OB and RE3-OB; cartservice -> redis is documented only (Redis calls are not traced).

frontend.description: Web frontend: serves the shop's HTTP pages and calls most backends for every page view. All user traffic enters here.

adservice.description: Serves text ads for product and cart pages.

cartservice.description: Stores and retrieves the items in users' carts, in redis.

checkoutservice.description: Places orders: fetches the cart, prices the items, charges the card, ships, sends the confirmation e-mail and empties the cart.

currencyservice.description: Converts prices between currencies; the busiest service (called for every displayed price).

paymentservice.description: Charges credit cards (mock) and returns a transaction id.

productcatalogservice.description: Lists, searches and returns products from a JSON catalogue; called by frontend, checkoutservice and recommendationservice.

recommendationservice.description: Recommends products for the cart; queries productcatalogservice.

shippingservice.description: Quotes shipping costs and ships orders (mock).

redis.description: redis-cart: the cart store behind cartservice.

telemetry_names.frontend-external: the external LoadBalancer Service in front of frontend; its metrics describe traffic reaching frontend, not a separate workload
telemetry_names.main: an unidentified container in the RCAEval telemetry, not part of the Online Boutique architecture
telemetry_names.frontend-check: an unidentified container in the RCAEval telemetry, not part of the Online Boutique architecture
telemetry_names.PassthroughCluster: an Istio/Envoy virtual cluster (traffic to destinations outside the mesh), not a service
telemetry_names.InboundPassthroughClusterIpv4: an Istio/Envoy virtual cluster (inbound traffic without a matching service), not a service
telemetry_names.istio-init: the Istio sidecar's init container (sets up traffic redirection when a pod starts), not a service

notes: In RCAEval's traces, adservice, cartservice and shippingservice record no spans of their own: their latency and errors show up only in their callers' client spans, e.g. frontend's hipstershop.CartService/GetCart.
A load generator (not in the telemetry) drives the traffic through frontend.
Span status codes are gRPC codes (0 = OK); a few spans carry HTTP codes.
